summary.text: A 55-year-old man presented with progressive voice change and a throat-blocking sensation while swallowing solids and liquids for three months, with a dry cough but no fever, cold or systemic illness. He was conscious, oriented and afebrile, weighed 65 kg, had no pallor, clubbing, cyanosis or lymphadenopathy, systemic examination was unremarkable, and he was ASA Grade 2.

High-resolution CT of the neck showed a mildly enhancing polypoidal lesion arising from the left posterior oropharyngeal wall, displacing the tongue and epiglottis. Cardiologic evaluation gave an ejection fraction of 67% with an interatrial septal aneurysm and low anesthetic risk, while pulmonary function tests showed severe obstruction and high risk per the pulmonologist.

He underwent awake nasal fiberoptic intubation with topical anaesthesia and blocks, then general anesthesia and marsupialization of the cyst lasting about 90 minutes with 20 ml blood loss. He was extubated without complications, observed for two days, and had an uneventful, complete recovery.

summary.text: A 48-year-old man presented with a 15-day history of dysphagia and throat pain and two months of dysphonia, with no significant past medical history. He was alert, afebrile and hemodynamically stable with Mallampati class II, three-finger mouth opening, unrestricted neck movement and ASA Grade 2.

Video laryngoscopy showed a cystic lesion of about 4×3 cm arising from the left vallecula and attached posteriorly to the epiglottis, and contrast-enhanced CT of the neck showed a well-defined peripherally enhancing cystic lesion at the left vallecula.

After awake nasal fiberoptic intubation with topical anaesthesia and blocks, he underwent partial epiglottectomy under general anesthesia lasting 130 minutes. Recovery was smooth and he was extubated after regaining adequate respiratory effort without complications.

summary.text: A 52-year-old man presented with a six-week history of persistent globus sensation, mild difficulty swallowing solid food and intermittent hoarseness, denying respiratory distress, stridor, fever or systemic symptoms. He weighed 72 kg with stable vital signs, Mallampati class III, full neck mobility and normal cardiovascular, respiratory and abdominal evaluations; he was ASA Grade 2.

Flexible nasopharyngoscopy showed a smooth cystic swelling of about 3.5 cm from the right vallecular region partially obscuring the epiglottis, and contrast-enhanced CT of the neck showed a well-defined fluid-density lesion consistent with a vallecular cyst.

Awake nasal fiberoptic intubation was performed via the left nostril with a size 6.5 flexometallic tube, followed by endoscopic excision under general anesthesia lasting about 75 minutes with 30 ml blood loss and no intraoperative complications. He was extubated after reversal, discharged on postoperative day three with complete symptom resolution and no recurrence at follow-up.
